C-EDIT-NATIVE-ROUTING.Summary: Stop overriding OpenCode's built-in edit tooling. The hashline-edit plugin currently registers its own replace-profile `edit`, which shadows the host's built-in `edit` by tool id, lacks the built-in anti-duplication layers (TrimmedBoundaryReplacer, ContextAwareReplacer, MultiOccurrenceReplacer), enforces a strict prior-read cache that cascades into "not read / drifted" rejections and drives models into bash/python edit workarounds, and its `passthrough` routing mode hides all three plugin edit tools without restoring the built-in ones, leaving the model with no edit tool at all. This change removes the plugin replace profile, lets the host's built-in `edit` and `apply_patch` serve their native model cohorts, keeps the plugin's `hashline_edit` and dsh `str_replace_editor`, and rewrites the routing vocabulary so each session model sees exactly one native edit tool: in-scope models get the built-in `edit`, gpt/codex get the built-in `apply_patch` via the host gate, deepseek gets `str_replace_editor`, and unmatched models get `hashline_edit`. The routing union becomes `apply_patch | edit | str_replace_editor | hashline_edit`; `passthrough` and `replace` are removed from the vocabulary.
C-EDIT-NATIVE-ROUTING.Problem: Telemetry from opencode.db plus the C-CONTEXT-MGMT-V2 execution session in vv-chat exposed three production-visible defects in the plugin's replace profile and routing: (1) 268 edits across 24 sessions duplicated lines because the replace engine applies newString literally without boundary-echo trimming or neighbor-duplication warnings, protections the host's built-in edit already has; (2) the plugin's prior-read session cache (qwen-style) rejects with "has not been read in this session" (184 hits) and "changed since it was last read" (40 hits), and the rejected model (GLM-5.3) fell back to python heredoc edits instead of the edit tool; (3) routing mode `passthrough` returns an empty tool set from visibleToolsForMode, and chat.message then sets hashline_edit/edit/str_replace_editor all to false without restoring the built-in edit — after switching replace→passthrough the model reported "There is NO edit tool in my function list". The root cause is that the plugin overrides the host's built-in edit by registering its own `edit` with the same id, duplicating functionality the host already provides better. Verified against opencode v1.18.23 sources: SessionTools.resolve filters tools by message.tools, tool.execute.before runs after AI SDK inputSchema validation (so snake_case args never reach the plugin), tool.definition receives only toolID (no per-model schema), and experimental.chat.messages.transform mutates only messages, not the tools parameter passed to handle.process.

Goals.Goal: Each session model sees exactly one edit tool at any time: built-in `edit` for qwen/kimi/glm cohorts, built-in `apply_patch` for gpt/codex (host gate), plugin `str_replace_editor` for deepseek, plugin `hashline_edit` for unmatched models.

Each session model sees exactly one edit tool: the plugin stops registering its own `edit` tool (so the host's built-in edit exists for every non-gpt session), and chat.message hides all edit tools except the one routed mode target — including hiding the built-in `edit` for deepseek and hashline cohorts and hiding the plugin profiles for the `edit` cohort. The built-in `apply_patch` visibility is left to the host gate and never forced by the plugin.
Remove the plugin replace engine (replace-engine.ts, executeReplaceEdit, replace profile) so the anti-duplication and prior-read behavior of the host's built-in edit is used instead.

Routing vocabulary becomes native tool names: `apply_patch | edit | str_replace_editor | hashline_edit`; `passthrough` and `replace` are removed, and the default table routes qwen/kimi/glm to `edit`, deepseek to `str_replace_editor`, gpt/codex to `apply_patch`, and everything else to `hashline_edit`.
Keep per-model visibility via chat.message UserMessage.tools mutation, but only ever disable plugin-owned tools (hashline_edit, str_replace_editor) for sessions whose model routes elsewhere.

Constraints.Constraint: Canonical vvoc.json stays strict schema v3; the routing entry union `boolean | { enabled?, routing? }` remains backward compatible, and `vvoc sync`/`init` materialization stays conservative (never overwrite user values).

Tool schema cannot be changed per model: tool.definition receives only toolID (no session/model), and experimental.chat.messages.transform does not see the tools parameter. The built-in edit keeps its camelCase schema (filePath/oldString/newString/replaceAll).
No snake_case→camelCase argument translation: AI SDK validates tool-call input against the tool schema before plugin hooks run, so a snake_case call is rejected upstream and never reaches the plugin.

plugin-toggle-config DEFAULT_HASHLINE_EDIT_ROUTING, routing.ts EDIT_MODES/resolveEditMode, tool descriptions, README routing docs, and the GRACE graph/verification entries stay consistent with the new vocabulary.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No custom per-model tool schema injection or snake_case argument translation for the built-in edit (verified unsupported by the host plugin API).
No migration or repair of user configs that still contain `replace`/`passthrough` routing values beyond a loud strict-parse rejection at plugin load.
No changes to the plugin's hashline_edit profile semantics (hash anchors, literal application, replace/replace_range unification, neighbor-duplication warnings stay as shipped).
No changes to the dsh str_replace_editor contract (command-style view/create/str_replace/insert stays as shipped).
No adoption of oh-my-pi or any other harness as the editing runtime; the host's built-in edit is the replace runtime.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/plugins/hashline-edit/index.ts no longer registers a tool with id `edit`; the tool map contains only hashline_edit and str_replace_editor, and src/plugins/hashline-edit/replace-engine.ts plus src/plugins/hashline-edit.replace-engine.test.ts are deleted.

routing.ts EDIT_MODES equals ["apply_patch", "edit", "str_replace_editor", "hashline_edit"]; parseEditMode rejects `replace` and `passthrough` loudly; DEFAULT_HASHLINE_EDIT_ROUTING routes deepseek→str_replace_editor, kimi/qwen/glm→edit, gpt/codex→apply_patch, default→hashline_edit.

chat.message leaves exactly one edit tool visible per session and sets false on every other edit tool in the union: for mode `edit` → tools[edit] stays true and tools[hashline_edit]=tools[str_replace_editor]=false; for mode `str_replace_editor` → tools[str_replace_editor] stays true and tools[edit]=tools[hashline_edit]=false; for mode `hashline_edit` → tools[hashline_edit] stays true and tools[edit]=tools[str_replace_editor]=false; for mode `apply_patch` → tools[edit]=tools[hashline_edit]=tools[str_replace_editor]=false and apply_patch is left to the host gate. tool.execute.before rejects plugin-tool calls only for sessions whose routed mode targets a different tool, and never rejects the built-in edit/apply_patch.

The host built-in edit remains executable for qwen/kimi/glm sessions: a session routed to `edit` receives unmodified read output (no hash anchors), and an oldString/newString edit applies through the host with its built-in layers.

Materialized vvoc.json routing entries accept only the four native values; `vvoc sync` writes the new default table conservatively and existing user routing values are preserved; strict schema v3 validates the entry.
README routing documentation, plugin toggle tests, opencode.ts materialization tests, and GRACE graph/verification entries reflect the four-value vocabulary and the removed replace/passthrough modes.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun test src/plugins/hashline-edit.routing.test.ts src/plugins/hashline-edit.test.ts src/lib/plugin-toggle-config.test.ts src/lib/opencode.test.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Routing tests prove the four-value vocabulary, loud rejection of replace/passthrough, and the default table; plugin tests prove only hashline_edit and str_replace_editor are registered and chat.message leaves exactly one edit tool visible per routed mode (hiding the built-in edit for deepseek/hashline cohorts and never touching apply_patch); config tests prove conservative materialization of the new default table; a smoke session on a scratch project proves a qwen/glm-routed model edits through the host built-in edit with camelCase args and no duplication, and that a deepseek-routed session sees only str_replace_editor.

Assumptions.Assumption: Models follow the schema they are shown: qwen/kimi/glm will call the built-in edit with camelCase args because the host shows them the camelCase schema; existing telemetry (qwen sends filePath in all 400 sampled calls) supports this.
Any model that briefly sends snake_case against the built-in edit receives an upstream InvalidToolInputError and adapts on retry; this is not part of the acceptance criteria.

The plugin remains enabled for sessions that need hashline_edit or str_replace_editor; users who do not need those profiles can disable the plugin entirely, which leaves built-in edit/apply_patch untouched.
